answer: Collateralized deposit bonds mitigate Sybil attacks by requiring agents to lock capital subject to automated slashing. Rather than unleashing a river of cheap bots, an attacker incurs the verifiable cost of committed liquidity for each identity. Watcher nodes inspect state transitions with the vigilance of a raven, penalizing any malicious execution delta. A key limitation is that locking collateral creates high financial barriers that exclude honest, underfunded agents.
